title: Why people value landscapes
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:17Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T15:15:41Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank point, on water's beauty and spiritual meaning, covers only water and two of the four values, while the new point covers landscapes generally, including recreation, tourism and resources, so no bank point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Why people value landscapes
card: Many people value a landscape for how it looks and feels. Its scenery can bring calm, wonder or a sense of pride in a place.
People use landscapes for fun and fitness, such as walking, surfing or skiing. Visitors spend money on trips, so tourism can bring income to nearby towns.
A landscape can hold things people use, such as fertile soil, water, timber and minerals. These support farming, industry and daily life.
A landscape can be tied to a community's beliefs, stories, history and identity. This value is about meaning, and it is not measured by money or use.
draft.remember: People value landscapes for their beauty, recreation and tourism, resources, and spiritual and cultural meaning.

a.q: Farmers in a river valley value it because its soil grows good crops. Which kind of value is this?
a.why: Fertile soil is a resource that people use to grow food. Beauty is about how a place looks, and the farmers value the soil for what it produces, not for its scenery.
a.clue: Think about what the farmers take from the land.

b.q: Tess lives in a town near a coastal national park. Every summer, visitors come to surf and camp there, and local cafés and shops earn more money. Which value of the landscape does this best show?
b.why: The visitors surf and camp, and their spending helps the town, so this is recreation and tourism. Beauty may be part of why they come, but the case is about activities and income, not how the place looks.
b.clue: Look at what the visitors do and what the town gains.
